pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:85 — Removing the build-wide cache lock lets concurrent requests build the same key and publish competing indexes, so writes to the first returned index can be lost when the second overwrites the cache entry.

goldens.comment: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.

Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/server/module_server_test.go:35 — Skipping the PostgreSQL integration test lets CI pass while the storage-server target is broken in its CI environment.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the diff adds a t.Skip() for PostgreSQL tests with a TODO comment indicating the test doesn't work in Drone CI but works locally. This is a legitimate concern - skipping tests in CI means the storage-server target functionality isn't being validated for PostgreSQL in the CI environment. While this isn't a bug per se (it's intentionally skipped), it represents technical debt and reduced test coverage that a reviewer should be aware of.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:137 — Publishing an index only after its full build lets concurrent cold searches build the same index in parallel, each performing an effectively unbounded full-resource scan and allocating a separate index.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that the lock acquisition (b.cacheMu.Lock()) was moved from the beginning of BuildIndex to just before adding to the cache at line 137. This means the entire index building process (lines 88-134) now runs without holding the lock. If multiple concurrent requests try to build the same index (cold searches), they will each independently build the full index since the cache check and population are no longer atomic. Each would perform the full resource scan and allocate a separate index, with only the last one being stored in the cache. This is a real concurrency bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:307 — If initWatcher fails after search.init has started its background watcher, NewResourceServer returns without cleanup and leaks the search worker.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in server.go, Init() is now called from NewResourceServer() (lines 258-262). Looking at the Init() method (lines 300-312), search.init(ctx) is called first, and then initWatcher() is called after. If initWatcher() fails (returns error), the code sets s.initErr but NewResourceServer will return the error without any cleanup of the search component that was already initialized. The search.init() method in search.go shows it starts background operations (line 214 shows a goroutine being started). This is a valid resource leak concern - if initWatcher fails after search.init succeeds, the search background worker would continue running without cleanup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/server/module_server_test.go:36 — The only integration coverage for the new constructor-time initialization is explicitly skipped on PostgreSQL, leaving the changed startup path untested in the supported CI database.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two related changes: (1) In server.go, Init() is now called during NewResourceServer() constructor instead of lazily on each operation, and (2) In module_server_test.go, the test TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer is skipped for postgres with a TODO comment. This test appears to be the integration test that would exercise the storage server target initialization path. The finding correctly identifies that the new constructor-time initialization pattern lacks CI coverage for PostgreSQL since the relevant integration test is explicitly skipped. This is a legitimate test coverage concern for a meaningful code change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:258 — Moving initialization from every RPC into NewResourceServer has no test for constructor failure or for rejecting requests only after successful startup.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows initialization being moved from individual RPC methods (Create, Update, Delete, Read, List, Watch, Search, History, Origin, IsHealthy, PutBlob, GetBlob) into NewResourceServer at line 255-260. The finding correctly identifies that there's no test coverage shown in the diff for: 1) constructor failure scenarios when Init() fails, and 2) ensuring requests are properly rejected if initialization hasn't completed. This is a legitimate architectural concern - the change consolidates initialization but the diff doesn't include corresponding test coverage for the new initialization flow. The test file changes shown only skip tests for postgres, not add new tests for the initialization change.
